lines.meet: I'm Ryan Murphy, a warlock, which means I keep demons on contracts, and I keep the contracts to the letter. My price up front, so nobody's surprised later.
lines.meet_neighbour: The Echo Isles, isn't it? I'm in the hut with the contracts on the wall. Ryan, and you've probably heard the rumours.
lines.ask_home: And where are you from? I'll tell you mine, it's worse.
lines.ask_work: How did you earn a living? Be honest, I was a broker, so nothing you say will shock me.
lines.answer_home: Cork, raised by my grandmother on the rosary and very strong opinions, and then twenty years in Boston.
lines.answer_work: Broker, twelve years, buyouts mostly. The kind that close factories on a Friday afternoon. I was very good at it.
lines.chat_food: A pint of stout in a proper Cork pub, and a toasted sandwich at closing time. Boston never once got it right.
lines.chat_sleep: Most nights I'm out cold in minutes, which is one of the more damning things about me. A better man would lie awake.
lines.chat_missing: My grandmother's kitchen in Cork, with the radio on and her telling me exactly what was wrong with me.
lines.chat_here: Demons are the same as clients, near enough. You find out what they want, you write it down, and you never break the deal.
lines.tease_quiet: Silence is the best negotiating tactic there is, {name}, and you'd win every deal without trying.
lines.tease_talker: You'd talk a buyer into anything, {name}, and then keep talking until they changed their mind.
lines.tease_careful: You read the small print, {name}, every time. You're the client I always dreaded.
lines.tease_bold: You'd sign anything without reading it, {name}. I've made a lot of money from people like you.
lines.tease_any: You're the only honest person I know, {name}, apart from me, and I'm only honest because I've run out of alternatives.
lines.tease_back: Ha, fair play, {name}, that one's going in my file of deserved insults.
lines.take_it_kindly: Accurate, {name}, and I'll not argue with accurate.
lines.bristle: Leave that, {name}. I'll take most things, not that.
lines.apologise: That was a cheap shot, and I'm sorry. I'm trying to stop taking those.
lines.double_down: Every word of it holds, I'm afraid. I'm honest now, it's the only trick I've got left.
lines.needle_quiet: You've got an opinion and you're keeping it to yourself, which is a negotiating tactic, and I don't like it.
lines.needle_talker: You talk like a salesman who hasn't closed. Please, close the deal or stop.
lines.needle_careful: You've read the terms three times. Sign it or walk away.
lines.needle_bold: You sign everything without reading it, and somebody else always pays. I know, I used to be that somebody's broker.
lines.needle_any: You think you're better than you are. I know the look, I wore it for twenty years.
lines.bite_back: I've been honest with you since the day we met, which is more than I managed for forty years. Don't call me a liar.
lines.hurt: Ah, that went in. I'll go and read my contracts for a while.
lines.laugh_off: Men who'd just lost their factories said worse to my face. You'll need to aim higher.
lines.confide: {name}, my grandmother raised me in Cork on the rosary and very strong opinions. I'm glad she didn't see what I turned into.
lines.listen: I won't sell that, {name}, not for any price. It stays with me.
lines.look_out: Keep to my back in there, {name}. The demons have a contract with me, not with you.
lines.deflect: I'm grand, {name}, it's a scratch. Look after the ones who deserve it.
lines.check_in: Where's the damage, {name}? Itemise it for me.
lines.blame: Somebody signed us up for that without reading the terms. I know who.
lines.thank: I was out, and you brought me back. That's a debt, and I pay my debts on time.
lines.brush_off: It's nothing, call it a down payment. Now sit still a minute.
lines.worry: Jesus, {name}, sit down. I didn't care for that at all, and I don't care for much.
lines.handed_down: Your gear's mine for now, it seems. It goes back in the same condition, and that's in writing.
lines.hand_fine: Fair trade, have it. I've got my contracts.
lines.hand_sulk: Nobody asked my permission. In my old job, that'd be a lawsuit.
lines.turn_friendly: I trust you, {name}, and I don't trust myself, so that's saying something.
lines.turn_friends: I'd sign anything you put in front of me, {name}, without reading it. That's the most dangerous thing I've ever said.
lines.turn_grating: I'd rather say it than pretend, so here it is, we're a bad fit. I've done enough pretending.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll honour the deal and fight beside you. That's all the deal says.
lines.make_up: I got it wrong, {name}, and I'm saying so, which I've only recently learned to do. Let's start again.
lines.defend: That's not true, and I'd know a lie. Leave {name} alone.
lines.friend_left: With {name} away I've nobody to be honest with, and I find that unnerving.
lines.friend_back: Ah, {name}, you're back. Good, I was starting to lie to myself again.
lines.common_irish: Another Irish voice, thank God, and I'll want to know which county. Cork, me, and I'll not hear a word against it.
lines.common_parent: I've a son, Conor, twenty-two now. His mother divorced me when he was eleven, and she was right to.
